First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int {b}^{\,px+q}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{p\operatorname{ln}⁡(b)}{b}^{\,px+q}+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{2}^{3x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{1}{2}^{3x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{2}^{3x}}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}]}_{a}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[{2}^{3x}]}_{a}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(8-{2}^{3a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot (8-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{2}^{3a})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={2}^{3x}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{2}^{3x}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{2}^{3x}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042659/assets/c2af905a46cea7b7512a727a5e53a2a178e4902f7114f86439365684e6685efa.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{2}^{3x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot (8-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{2}^{3a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot (8-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}.\end{aligned}
$$
